On a phone: Names become one sideways-scrolling row at 22px with scroll-snap, the selected one in full ink. Beneath, the stage fills the width and is 70svh tall; the sheet keeps its true size, anchored top-left with a 16px inset and cropped by the stage's right and bottom edges. Tapping a name swaps it.

Adjusted for this page:
- It names colours (white): map them onto this palette's roles (ground `--bg`, panels `--surface` and the fields, text `--ink`/`--muted`, the accent `--accent` on the primary action only).

### 3. how-it-works — Call and response column (list)
The sequence is shown as what you give and what comes back, in one narrow column 560px wide starting at column 4, or on the page's text axis. Three exchanges, 88px apart. Each opens with a sentence at 20px medium that begins with its order word ('First, install it.' 'Then ask for a chart.'). 16px under it, the call: the literal thing the user enters, in a filled panel one tone off the ground, radius 8px, padding 20px. For a developer tool that is real code in `<pre><code>` at 14px with a working copy button; otherwise it is the product's own input holding real typed text. Under the call, indented 56px, the response: a true-size fragment marked data-ui showing what the product returns. The third response is the finished result and breaks out of the column, 760px wide, running to column 12. The heading, two to four words at 28px, sits 56px above the first sentence.
On a phone: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Calls and responses stack without the indent; a 24px gap and a lighter panel tone set the response apart. Code panels scroll sideways inside themselves. The final result runs edge to edge at true size, cropped on the right if wider.

Adjusted for this page:
- It names its own corners: use the one radius of this page (square unless the direction says otherwise) and one button shape.

### 4. proof — Recognition as a table (table)
Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
On a phone: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

Adjusted for this page:
- It draws lines or borders: keep them only inside a table, a form or a `data-ui` fragment; elsewhere separate with space or a change of ground.

## 8. Motion — Masked headline
On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.
This is the signature move, the one loud moment. Around it the page still needs the rest of the motion layer (SKILL.md step 9): an entrance for the parts of every section, feedback on every control, and one moving picture. The inspector fails a page that barely moves. Recipes: references/motion.md.

## 9. Where the richness comes from
The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.

## 10. How this direction goes wrong
The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

## 11. Real references
Studied sites that work this way. Take the principle, never the specifics: no names, copy, images or signature assets of theirs.
- **Applied Imagination** (One Page Love, studied score 8.3) `opl-applied-imagination`
  Idea: An essay conceived on a flight is read as a descent: an altimeter ticks from 30,000 ft to zero while you scroll down through halftone clouds to mountains at ground level.
  Hero: A pale blue sky fading to warm cream fills the viewport, with white clouds shaded in halftone dots. A tiny serif logotype sits top-centre; no nav. The title, two centred lines of black wedge-serif at 8.9vw, occupies the middle half of the screen and about 73% of its width; a cloud layer passes in front of the second line's baseline so the feet of the letters dissolve into dots. A two-line centred deck at 24px sits beneath. A mono byline strip is centred on the bottom edge with a scroll cue bottom-right. On the left edge at mid-height, a short vertical rule carries a two-line mono altitude readout.
  Worth taking: Tie a persistent numeric readout to scroll position (altitude falling to zero) so the reader's progress becomes part of the story.
- **The Queue** (One Page Love, studied score 8.1) `opl-the-queue`
  Idea: An essay on queueing where the queue is the ornament: a line of drawn figures stands along the bottom of the hero and returns between chapters in changing period dress.
  Hero: Pinkish warm-grey page. A 12px mono breadcrumb sits top-left; there is no other navigation. The two-word title is set in a light serif at 200px (14vw), centred, its middle slightly above the viewport centre, spanning about 60% of the width with tight tracking. One centred line of grey 20px serif sits 40px beneath. The lower third stays empty until a single row of about 25 small greyscale drawn figures, each around 110px tall, stands on a hairline rule 20px above the bottom edge and runs the full width like a frieze.

Adjusted for this page:
- It sets text at 10px: use your small step (13px or more) instead.
- It draws lines or borders: keep them only inside a table, a form or a `data-ui` fragment; elsewhere separate with space or a change of ground.

### 3. how-it-works — Pinned fragment, changing state (pinned)
Two columns. Right, columns 7–12: a stage that is position: sticky; top: 14vh, holding one fragment of the real interface at true size on a single flat stage colour, about 520px square. Left, columns 1–5: three statements, each in its own block 80vh tall, so one is in view at a time. A statement is a two-line sentence at 28–32px that begins with its order word ('Paste a link.', 'Then pick the parts you want.', 'Share it when it looks right.') plus one supporting line at 16px. The statement nearest the viewport's centre is in full ink; the others sit at 30%. As each statement becomes active the fragment changes to the matching state: an empty field, a filled list with two rows selected, a finished result with its confirmation. Build the states in HTML and switch a class; do not swap screenshots. The heading, two to four words at 24–28px, sits above the first statement.
On a phone: The stage is sticky at the top, 46svh tall, the fragment fitted by cropping to its active region, not by shrinking its text. Statements scroll beneath it in blocks 60svh tall at 22px. The stage releases after the third statement.

Adjusted for this page:
- It fades text: anything a visitor reads, inactive items of a list included, is `--ink` or `--muted` at full strength (contrast 4.5:1 or more). The active item is told apart by `--ink` against `--muted`, weight or the accent, not by fading the rest.

### 4. proof — Plain names in columns (list)
A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
On a phone: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

## 8. Motion — Slow crossfade
The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.
This is the signature move, the one loud moment. Around it the page still needs the rest of the motion layer (SKILL.md step 9): an entrance for the parts of every section, feedback on every control, and one moving picture. The inspector fails a page that barely moves. Recipes: references/motion.md.

## 9. Where the richness comes from
Precision. With so little on the page, alignment, spacing and the exact size relationships are the design. Every element shares the column's left edge.

## 10. How this direction goes wrong
This is the one direction where a small headline is right; the inspector will not object, but do not mix it with a large display line. Emptiness must look decided: keep the column edges exact and the vertical rhythm even. Not suitable when the subject needs emotion or photography to sell. Quiet is not thin: the column must still deliver every piece of content the brief asks for, in full, at 16px or more in the full ink. In blind tests the quiet version lost every time it was quiet everywhere: a small headline beside an empty panel read as unfinished. Quiet means few things, not small things: the headline and the demonstration are large, and every screen holds content.

## 11. Real references
Studied sites that work this way. Take the principle, never the specifics: no names, copy, images or signature assets of theirs.
- **Gil Huybrecht** (Awwwards Site of the Day, studied score 7.6) `aww-gil-huybrecht`
  Idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
  Hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
  Worth taking: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
- **Cursor Compile** (One Page Love, studied score 8.3) `opl-compile`
  Idea: The event name drawn as seven looping one-line curves in seven colours, more signature than logotype, on an otherwise whisper-quiet off-white page whose images are re-rendered as rows of coloured characters.
  Hero: Warm off-white field with no header or navigation. Starting about 23% down, a line-drawn wordmark spans from 8% to 92% of the width and about 29% of the height: each letter is a single 2px stroke looping like a Lissajous figure, each in a different colour (orange, green, olive, lilac, black, brown, blue), overlapping its neighbours. Directly beneath, two 14px captions, one flush left in ink and one flush right in grey. After a gap of about 20% of the viewport, three equal columns sit at the bottom, each topped by a hairline: an 18px statement, a grey 14px paragraph, and an email field over a full-width near-black rectangular button.
  Worth taking: Draw the name as one continuous thin looping stroke per letter, each in a different colour, and let it be the only large element on the page.
- **Berd** (One Page Love, studied score 7.5) `opl-berd`
  Idea: The page types its own headlines into an empty app window, then hands over to toy-like 3D characters and ends on a giant red face delivering a joke testimonial.
  Hero: A warm light-grey field covered by a faint dot grid, with no navigation at first. Centred, a single rounded rectangle 1000px wide and 710px tall (70% of the width, 79% of the height) in a lighter grey, with three tiny traffic-light dots in its top-left corner: an empty application window. In its exact centre a headline at about 42px is typed one character at a time; the capture shows only its first letter. Nothing else is on screen. On scroll the window gives way to 90px words typing onto the bare grid with a cursor line, and a small logo and a black download tag pin to the top corners.
  Worth taking: Open on an empty application window and type the headline into it, so the first screen demonstrates the product's premise instead of describing it.

LoRA optimizes large models by constraining the updates to the pre-trained weight matrices during adaptation to a low-rank decomposition. Specifically, for a pre-trained weight matrix ( W_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k} ), the update is represented as a low-rank decomposition ( W_0 + \Delta W = W_0 + BA ), where ( B \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r} ) and ( A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times k} ), and the rank ( r \ll \min(d, k) ). During training, the pre-trained weight matrix ( W_0 ) is frozen and does not receive gradient updates, while the matrices ( A ) and ( B ) contain trainable parameters. This approach significantly reduces the number of trainable parameters compared to full fine-tuning, making the model more efficient in terms of both storage and computation.

### Root Cause Analysis & Fixes Both issues have been investigated, fixed, tested, and verified on the live system. --- ### Issue 1: Why in-text response citing appeared as plain text (`cite:2301.02419`) without highlight or icon #### Root Cause: 1. **ReactMarkdown Default Protocol Sanitization**: - In Markdown, `[cite:2301.02419](citation:2301.02419)` was generated by preprocessing. - However, ReactMarkdown's built-in URL sanitizer (micromark/mdast) only permits standard schemes (`http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, relative anchors). Any unrecognized custom URI scheme like `citation:` is deemed unsafe and stripped to an empty string (`href=""`). - Consequently, the custom link handler (`href.startsWith('citation:')`) did not trigger, falling back to a plain `cite:2301.02419` which rendered as unstyled plain text. #### Fix: 1. **Relative Hash URI Scheme**: Changed the markdown citation target to use a safe relative anchor: `[cite:${id}](#/citation/${id})`. 2. **Explicit `urlTransform={(url) => url}`**: Added `urlTransform` to `` in [ChatPanel.tsx](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/frontend_rag/components/ChatPanel.tsx#L279) to ensure custom schemes are never stripped. 3. **Multi-Scheme Interceptor**: ```tsx a({ href, children, ...props }) { if (href && (href.startsWith('citation:') || href.startsWith('#/citation/') || href.startsWith('#citation/'))) { const paperId = href.replace(/^(?:citation:|#\/citation\/|#citation\/)/, '').trim(); const info = getPaperDisplayInfo(paperId, msg.grounded_chunks, activeChunks, 34); return ( ); } return {children}; } ``` 4. **Existing Format Normalization**: Added a preprocessor rule to normalize any literal `cite:` text emitted by the model into the interactive button. --- ### Issue 2: Why "Paper 98" and "101" showed up as citations #### Root Cause: 1. **Internal Paper Bibliographies**: - The retrieved chunks for vision transformers included CVPR papers (`cvf_Zhang_...`, `cvf_Dong_...`). Inside the body text of those papers were citations to their own internal bibliography items, e.g. `[98]` and `[101]`. - The LLM copied those literal brackets (`[98]` and `[101]`) into its synthesis. 2. **Overly Permissive Extraction Regex**: - The citation regex previously made the `Paper:` prefix optional: `/`?\[(?:(?:Paper(?:\s*ID)?|arXiv)\s*:?\s*)?([a-zA-Z0-9._\/-]+)\]`?/gi` - Because `Paper:` was optional, the integer reference numbers `98` and `101` were extracted as paper IDs. - When the frontend attempted to resolve the title for ID `98`, no chunk had `paper_id: '98'`, falling back to `"Paper 98"`. #### Fix: 1. **Bibliography Number Filter (`^\d{1,4}$`)**: - Updated [rag.service.ts](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/backend_rag/src/rag/rag.service.ts#L96-L135) and [ChatPanel.tsx](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/frontend_rag/components/ChatPanel.tsx#L102-L165) with a strict integer filter: ```ts // Ignore bare bibliography reference numbers like [98], [101], [1], [2] if (/^\d{1,4}$/.test(id)) return; ``` 2. **Chunk ID & ArXiv Verification**: - A paper citation must either: - Have an explicit prefix: `[Paper: ]`, `[Paper ID: ]`, `[arXiv: ]` - Match a valid arXiv format: `^\d{4}\.\d{4,5}(?:v\d+)?$` - Match an OpenReview ID: `^openreview_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` - Match a CVF ID: `^cvf_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` - Match one of the retrieved `candidateChunks` 3. **Grounding Prompt Enforcement**: - Updated `STRICT_ACADEMIC_GROUNDING_PROMPT` Rule 3: > *"Cite each technique using `[Paper: {paper_id}]` matching the exact Paper ID in the excerpt header (e.g. `[Paper: 2301.02419]` or `[Paper: openreview_TTMyoOdB9hZ]`). Never cite internal bibliography numbers like [98] or [101] from inside the excerpt text."* --- ### Verification Results A live query was executed with: `"Explain parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques for vision transformers."` - **Extracted Citations**: ```json [ "2301.02419", "cvf_Dong_Low-Rank_Rescaled_Vision_Transformer_Fine-Tuning_A_Residual_Design_Approach_CVPR_2024_paper", "openreview_TTMyoOdB9hZ", "2606.10196" ] ``` - **Verification**: - `Paper 98` and `101` are completely eliminated. - All 4 cited papers map to their real publication titles in the UI. - In-text badges render with the `BookOpen` icon, truncated paper title, and paper ID pill, opening the chunk preview modal on click. --- ### Git Status All modifications are committed on your respective branches: - Backend: [`vuong/scientific-rag-backend`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/backend_rag) (`d0342d9`) - Frontend: [`vuong/scientific-rag-workbench`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/frontend_rag) (`d577647`) - Root: [`vuong/scientific-rag-fullstack`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS) (`c9af263`)

# Implementation Plan: Universal Hybrid Citation Engine for Scientific RAG

The current citation rendering mechanism fails when the local LLM outputs citations in parentheses (e.g. `(Paper ID: openalex:W4409626943)` or `(Paper ID: 2111.07624)`) instead of square brackets (`[Paper: ...]`). Furthermore, the model occasionally emits repeated tags (e.g. `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)`), or uses OpenAlex prefixes (`openalex:W4409626943`) which must be reliably recognized across both the frontend workbench and the backend telemetry.

This plan details the replacement of the fragile bracket-only approach with a **Universal Hybrid Citation Engine** that supports both bracketed and parenthesized forms, handles numeric source references `[1], [2]`, de-duplicates repeated adjacent citations, and guarantees consistent highlighting, paper title resolution, and modal chunk inspection.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No Breaking Changes to Backend Contracts**: The response format `{ query, answer, citations, grounded_chunks, latency_ms }` remains identical.
> Both backend and frontend will be enhanced to handle:
> 1. Parenthesized citations: `(Paper ID: <id>)`, `(Paper: <id>)`, `(openalex:<id>)`, `(arXiv:<id>)`.
> 2. Square bracket citations: `[Paper ID: <id>]`, `[Paper: <id>]`, `[openalex:<id>]`, `[arXiv:<id>]`, `[2111.07624]`.
> 3. Numeric source indexing: `[1]`, `[2]` mapped directly to retrieved chunks `topChunks[i - 1]`.
> 4. Automatic de-duplication: Consecutive repetitions like `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)` collapse into a single clean interactive badge.

---

## Architectural Comparison

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Current_Fragile_Flow ["Current Fragile Flow"]
        LLM1["Qwen2.5-7B Output"] -->|Outputs '(Paper ID: 2111.07624)'| Regex1["Bracket-only Regex `/[Paper: ...]/`"]
        Regex1 -->|MISSED! 0 citations found| PlainText["Rendered as raw unclickable text & empty footer"]
    end

    subgraph Proposed_Hybrid_Engine ["Universal Hybrid Citation Engine"]
        LLM2["Qwen2.5-7B Output"] --> ContextMap["Chunk Context Registry (IDs, Titles, Numeric Indices 1..N)"]
        ContextMap --> UniversalParser["Universal Multi-Syntax Normalizer (Parentheses, Brackets, OpenAlex, arXiv, [1..N])"]
        UniversalParser --> Deduplicator["Adjacent Citation De-duplicator"]
        Deduplicator --> MarkdownTransformer["Safe Anchor Normalizer `[cite:id](#/citation/id)`"]
        MarkdownTransformer --> UI["Interactive Academic Badge (Title + ID + BookOpen + Modal Preview)"]
        Deduplicator --> TelemetryFooter["Cited Sources Footer (All Unique Valid Papers with Titles)"]
    end
```

---

## Proposed Changes

### Component 1: Backend Grounding & Citation Extraction

#### [MODIFY] `backend_rag/src/rag/rag.service.ts`
- **Context Header Enhancement**:
  Provide both a numeric source index and the paper ID in the context block header:

  ```ts
  `3. MANDATORY CITATIONS: Every substantive technical claim, architectural detail, and performance metric must cite the exact paper using [Paper: {paper_id}] or [1], [2] matching the Source number or Paper ID in the excerpt headers. Do NOT repeat identical citation tags consecutively in the same sentence.`
  ```
- **Universal Multi-Syntax `extractCitations`**:
  Extend citation extraction to capture:
  1. Parentheses `(...)` and brackets `[...]` containing `Paper ID:`, `Paper:`, `arXiv:`, `openalex:`
  2. OpenAlex IDs `openalex:W...`
  3. arXiv decimal IDs `\d{4}\.\d{4,5}`
  4. OpenReview `openreview_...` and CVF `cvf_...`
  5. Source index references `[1]`, `[2]`, `Source 1`, `Source 2` mapped directly to `candidateChunks[index - 1].paper_id`
  6. Filter out bare non-index numbers, URLs, and generic punctuation.

---

### Component 2: Frontend Citation Preprocessor & Renderer

#### [MODIFY] `frontend_rag/components/ChatPanel.tsx`
- **Universal Regex Pattern**:
  Support both `[` and `(` delimiters, plus direct OpenAlex and arXiv strings:
  ```ts
  const UNIVERSAL_CITATION_REGEX = /`?([\[\(])\s*(?:(?:Paper(?:\s*ID)?|arXiv|Source)\s*:?\s*)?([^\]\)\n]+)\s*([\]\)])`?/gi;
  ```

  - When encountering `[1]`, `(1)`, `[Source 1]`, resolve to `indexToChunkMap.get(1)`.
  - When encountering `(Paper ID: 2111.07624)` or `[openalex:W4409626943]`, resolve to the matching chunk.
- **De-duplication of Consecutive Citations**:
  - Automatically collapse `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)` into a single distinct citation badge.
- **Title Truncation & Hover Tooltip**:

#### [MODIFY] `frontend_rag/app/page.tsx`
- **Fallback Chunk Enhancement**:

  - When it is arXiv (e.g. `2111.07624`), provide `https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07624`.

1: # Walkthrough — Next.js 16 Full-Stack Research Workbench Integration
2: 
3: ## 1. Executive Summary
4: 
5: We have built and verified the complete full-stack integration for the **Scientific Literature RAG System**, connecting the modern **Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4)** frontend workbench to the **NestJS 11** backend.
6: 
7: ### Key Highlights:
8: 1. **Next.js 16 API Proxy Architecture**:
9:    - Implemented server-to-server proxy handlers in `frontend_rag/app/api/rag/chat/route.ts` and `frontend_rag/app/api/rag/health/route.ts`.
10:    - Eliminates browser CORS configuration complexities while exposing unified endpoints.
11: 2. **Side-by-Side Research Workbench Layout**:
12:    - **Left Column**: Conversational chat interface with quick-start scientific question pills, LaTeX equation rendering (`remark-math`, `rehype-katex`), interactive citation badges (`[Paper: {paper_id}]`), and pipeline parameter controls (`top_k`, arXiv categories, PageRank boost).
13:    - **Right Column**: Collapsible grounded chunks inspector visualizing cosine similarity ($85\%$) vs author PageRank authority ($15\%$) score bars, section titles, and source paper chunk texts.
14: 3. **Paper Deep-Dive Inspector Modal**:
15:    - Clicking any citation badge or chunk card triggers an inspection modal with author metadata, full content, and direct links to arXiv (`https://arxiv.org/abs/{paper_id}`).
16: 4. **Live End-to-End Verification**:
17:    - Sent test query from `http://localhost:3000/api/rag/chat`.
18:    - Executed full RAG grounding over **913,205 vectors in LanceDB** and synthesized an answer using **local Qwen2.5-7B on NVIDIA CUDA GPU (RTX 4060)** in **13.2 seconds**.
19:

# Walkthrough — Next.js 16 Full-Stack Research Workbench Integration

## 1. Executive Summary

We have built and verified the complete full-stack integration for the **Scientific Literature RAG System**, connecting the modern **Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4)** frontend workbench to the **NestJS 11** backend, enhanced with the **Universal Hybrid Citation Engine**.

### Key Highlights:
1. **Next.js 16 API Proxy Architecture**:
   - Implemented server-to-server proxy handlers in `frontend_rag/app/api/rag/chat/route.ts` and `frontend_rag/app/api/rag/health/route.ts`.
   - Eliminates browser CORS configuration complexities while exposing unified endpoints.
2. **Universal Hybrid Citation Engine**:
   - **Multi-Syntax Support**: Seamlessly parses both square brackets (`[Paper ID: ...]`, `[Paper: ...]`, `[openalex:...]`, `[2111.07624]`) and parentheses (`(Paper ID: ...)`, `(Paper: ...)`, `(openalex:...)`, `(2111.07624)`).
   - **Numeric Source Indexing**: Reliably resolves `[1]`, `[2]`, `Source 1`, `(1)` to the corresponding retrieved candidate chunks.
   - **Representative Paper Titles**: Replaced bare numbers with real publication titles (e.g. `Industrial applications of large language models... [openalex:W4409626943]`).
   - **Adjacent Citation De-duplication**: Automatically collapses repeated sequential tags (e.g., `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)`) into a single distinct interactive chip.
   - **Bibliography Number Filtering**: Strictly filters out bare numbers like `[98]` and `[101]` copied from paper bibliographies.
   - **Multi-Provider Direct Routing**: Direct outbound navigation for arXiv (`arxiv.org/abs/...`), OpenAlex (`openalex.org/...`), OpenReview (`openreview.net/forum?...`), and CVF Open Access.
3. **Side-by-Side Research Workbench Layout**:
   - **Left Column**: Conversational chat interface with quick-start scientific question pills, LaTeX equation rendering (`remark-math`, `rehype-katex`), interactive citation badges, and pipeline parameter controls (`top_k`, arXiv categories, PageRank boost).
   - **Right Column**: Collapsible grounded chunks inspector visualizing cosine similarity ($85\%$) vs author PageRank authority ($15\%$) score bars, section titles, and source paper chunk texts.
4. **Paper Deep-Dive Inspector Modal**:
   - Clicking any citation badge or chunk card triggers an inspection modal with author metadata, full content, and direct provider links.

---

## 2. Full-Stack Dataflow Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Researcher
    participant UI as Next.js 16 UI (:3000)
    participant NextAPI as Next.js API Proxy (/api/rag/*)
    participant NestAPI as NestJS Backend (:8000)
    participant Lakehouse as LanceDB (913,205 Vectors)
    participant LLM as node-llama-cpp (RTX 4060 CUDA)

    User->>UI: Types research query ("Attention mechanism")
    UI->>NextAPI: POST /api/rag/chat { query, top_k, category, use_authority_boost }
    NextAPI->>NestAPI: Forward server-to-server POST :8000/api/rag/chat
    
    rect rgb(240, 248, 255)
        NestAPI->>Lakehouse: ANN Vector Cosine Search (768-D Nomic Embed)
        Lakehouse-->>NestAPI: Candidate chunks with distance
        NestAPI->>NestAPI: Hybrid Reranking (0.85 Sim + 0.15 PageRank)
    end

    rect rgb(250, 240, 255)
        NestAPI->>LLM: Generate Grounded Answer (Indexed Sources 1..N)
        LLM-->>NestAPI: Answer text with [Source N] or (Paper ID: {id}) citations
        NestAPI->>NestAPI: Universal Citation Extraction (Brackets + Parentheses + OpenAlex + Indices)
    end

    NestAPI-->>NextAPI: 200 OK JSON (answer, citations, grounded_chunks, latency_ms)
    NextAPI-->>UI: 200 OK JSON
    UI->>UI: Universal Preprocessing, De-duplication, & In-text Title Badges
```

---

## 3. UI Component Roster

| Component | File Path | Functionality |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`Navbar`** | [`frontend_rag/components/Navbar.tsx`](frontend_rag/components/Navbar.tsx) | Live telemetry badges: LanceDB chunk counter, LLM status, GPU hardware indicator, link to Swagger documentation. |
| **`ChatPanel`** | [`frontend_rag/components/ChatPanel.tsx`](frontend_rag/components/ChatPanel.tsx) | Chat scroll area, LaTeX markdown math rendering, Universal Hybrid Citation badges with title & ID, cited sources footer. |
| **`GroundedInspector`** | [`frontend_rag/components/GroundedInspector.tsx`](frontend_rag/components/GroundedInspector.tsx) | Collapsible right sidebar detailing all grounded chunks, score bars, and section anchors. |
| **`PaperModal`** | [`frontend_rag/components/PaperModal.tsx`](frontend_rag/components/PaperModal.tsx) | Deep-dive modal preview for inspected papers with direct routing to arXiv, OpenAlex, OpenReview, and CVF. |
| **`Root Page`** | [`frontend_rag/app/page.tsx`](frontend_rag/app/page.tsx) | Workbench orchestrator coordinating messages, health polling, chunk lookups, and fallback chunk metadata. |

---

## 4. Live Verification Results

### 4.1 Parenthesized & OpenAlex Query: `"Attention mechanism"`
- **Input Query**: `"Attention mechanism"` (`top_k = 5`)
- **Backend Citations Extracted**:
  - `openalex:W4409626943`
  - `2111.07624`
  - `2202.09556`
- **Frontend In-Text Badges**:
  - `(Paper ID: openalex:W4409626943)` ➔ `[BookOpen icon] Industrial applications of large language models... [openalex:W4409626943]`
  - `(Paper ID: 2111.07624)` ➔ `[BookOpen icon] Attention mechanisms in computer vision: A survey... [2111.07624]`
  - Consecutive duplicate `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)` ➔ Collapsed into a single badge.

### 4.2 Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Query
- **Input Query**: `"Explain parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques for vision transformers."`
- **Output**:
  - `2301.02419` (`Exploring Efficient Few-shot Adaptation for Vision Transformers`)
  - `cvf_Dong_...` (`Low-Rank Rescaled Vision Transformer Fine-Tuning: A Residual Design Approach`)
  - `openreview_TTMyoOdB9hZ` (`Important Channel Tuning`)
  - `2606.10196` (`Fisher-Guided Progressive Parameter Selection for Adaptive Fine-Tuning`)
  - Bibliography numbers `[98]` and `[101]` completely eliminated from citation lists.

---

## 5. Branch Governance
- Backend repository: `vuong/scientific-rag-backend` (`3c11d39`)
- Frontend repository: `vuong/scientific-rag-workbench` (`d93d9aa`)
- Full-stack superproject: `vuong/scientific-rag-fullstack` (`826e803`)

### Universal Hybrid Citation Engine — Complete Implementation Summary

The citation engine has been completely overhauled with a **Universal Hybrid Citation Engine** that eliminates inconsistencies between bracketed and parenthesized citations, OpenAlex identifiers, and repeated references.

---

### Key Capabilities Now Live

1. **Dual Delimiter Support (`[...]` and `(...)`)**:
   - The engine now treats square brackets and parentheses equivalently:
     - `(Paper ID: openalex:W4409626943)` ➔ `[BookOpen icon] Industrial applications of large language models... [openalex:W4409626943]`
     - `(Paper ID: 2111.07624)` ➔ `[BookOpen icon] Attention mechanisms in computer vision: A survey... [2111.07624]`
     - `[Paper: 2202.09556]` ➔ `[BookOpen icon] HDAM: Heuristic Difference Attention Module... [2202.09556]`

2. **Sequential Citation De-Duplication**:
   - When the model outputs repetitive citations in the same sentence (e.g. `(Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624, Paper ID: 2111.07624)`), the parser de-duplicates the batch and collapses adjacent identical badges into a **single clean interactive badge**.

3. **Perplexity-Style Source Indexing (`[1]`, `[2]`)**:
   - The context builder now presents excerpts as:
     `--- [Source 1 | Paper ID: 2111.07624 | Title: "Attention mechanisms..."] ---`
   - If the model cites `[1]`, `[2]`, or `(Source 1)`, the engine resolves the index directly to the corresponding candidate chunk's real paper title and ID.

4. **Multi-Provider Outbound Links**:
   - Clicking citation badges or chunk cards in the [PaperModal](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/frontend_rag/components/PaperModal.tsx) dynamically routes to the appropriate academic portal:
     - **OpenAlex**: `https://openalex.org/W4409626943`
     - **arXiv**: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07624`
     - **OpenReview**: `https://openreview.net/forum?id=...`
     - **CVF**: `https://openaccess.thecvf.com/`

5. **Strict Bibliography Index Filtering**:
   - Bare integers from internal paper bibliographies (e.g. `[98]`, `[101]`) are ignored, ensuring fake citations like `Paper 98` will never show up in the **Cited Sources** footer.

---

### Verification & Live Service Status
- **Backend**: Running on `http://localhost:8000` (`ready`, 99 GPU layers on RTX 4060 CUDA, 913,205 chunks in LanceDB).
- **Frontend**: Running on `http://localhost:3000` (`ready`).
- **Live Test Query**: `"Attention mechanism"` successfully extracted `openalex:W4409626943`, `2111.07624`, and `2202.09556` with 100% title mapping and click-to-preview modals.

### Branch Governance
All changes have been committed cleanly to your designated branches:
- Backend: [`vuong/scientific-rag-backend`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/backend_rag) (`3c11d39`)
- Frontend: [`vuong/scientific-rag-workbench`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS/frontend_rag) (`d93d9aa`)
- Full-Stack Root: [`vuong/scientific-rag-fullstack`](file:///C:/document/Study%20documents/backend_rag/RAG_TS) (`826e803`)

The full walkthrough is available in [walkthrough.md](file:///C:/Users/TDV/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/4db53373-1ab6-43ef-a7e9-7bb3fed98130/walkthrough.md).
